verdict.rationale: Checkout.com supports agentic/autonomous interactions primarily via webhooks (event-driven automation), idempotent retries, and its MCP server for AI-assisted operations (refunds, payment links, status queries) plus agentic-commerce integrations (ChatGPT, Google AI) where an AI agent can autonomously initiate payments. This gives partial infrastructure for background automations, but there's no documented workflow/orchestration engine, scheduler, or persistent autonomous 'automation' product akin to Zapier-like background jobs — the MCP server is framed as an IDE-assist tool requiring active developer interaction rather than a standing autonomous background process. Missing for 10: evidence of a dedicated automation/workflow-builder for unattended scheduled tasks, confirmation that MCP-driven actions can run without a human in the loop, and independent/hands-on validation of autonomous background operation.
